sessions.topic: First session of the year: what members shot over the break, upcoming schedule, reference links debate

turns.message: Good morning. Darkroom is open from 10. Quick note: the ventilation in the fix room was serviced this week, so the fumes should be more manageable than last time. Printing session runs until 1pm. next session: Saturday the 8th, 10am 🗓️

okay but I have been WAITING for this, did everyone actually shoot over the break or was it just me and Sol?? what did people get, what are you all printing today, and is there a critique slot or just darkroom time?? 😭🙏 also hi everyone missed you all so much

I had six sessions between Christmas and the new year. Three rolls of Kodak Tri-X 400, two of Ilford HP5 Plus 400. The light on the canal this time of year has qualities that reward patience. I will bring contact sheets.

anyway so the point is I went completely offscript with the pinhole thing @Bex @Callum, ended up doing a twelve-hour exposure on the fire escape and honestly?? highkey can't tell if it's ruined or incredible yet 🔥🔥
okay but a TWELVE HOUR exposure?? Sol I actually cannot 😭😭 that is genuinely wild and I need to see it immediately. lowkey this might be your best experiment yet and I am not even joking
cost per frame on 4x5 pinhole paper is basically zero if you cut your own. genuinely the most overlooked process in the group. lmk if you want the supplier I use 👍
I shot six frames on the coast during the break. Very Cartier-Bresson in the light, though not intentionally.

back from three weeks in Valencia. street work, which is what I default to when I'm somewhere unfamiliar. the question of what the image is asking of the viewer is harder when you don't speak the language. brought some contacts if anyone is interested.
Shot an industrial estate series near the ring road last week. From a compositional standpoint the geometry was more interesting than I expected.

Glad you made it back, Fen. Bex came to us through an open workshop I ran at the arts centre. She turned up with a contact sheet from a disposable that had more going on than most first rolls I see. Worth mentioning since people keep asking about the next open session. 🙂

okay but please don't make me sound talented when I barely knew what I was doing 😂 speaking of, I found this series by a Japanese photographer doing double exposure street work that is so relevant to what Sol's been trying. should I drop the link in here??

Bex, this chat is for members' own work, in my experience. Reference material belongs in the session discussion. The thing people miss about group chats is that external images tend to pull focus from what we are actually producing.
Otto I hear you but @Bex please send it to me separately because I genuinely do need to see it 😭 lowkey the chat rule is fair but also I have no self-control

My read on this is that the value of a session is rarely in the roll count. One considered frame outweighs twenty automatic ones. The pinhole exposure duration suggests that understanding regardless of format.
From a compositional standpoint, I rarely arrive at a location needing more than a single roll. Either the frame resolves or it does not. Volume does not change that.
Both useful framings of the same instinct. See everyone at 10 on Saturday. next session: Saturday the 8th, 10am 🗓️

sessions.topic: Darkroom prep, developer choices, scan-sharing proposal for absent members

turns.message: Morning. Fix trays are up. One reminder: run full fix times today. We had a short-fixed print last month and it affects archival stability. Developer is at 20 degrees. 🗓️

okay but who has the best developer right now?? Callum are you still on the homebrew formula?? and Otto what do you think about Xtol for pushing to 800?? I'm shooting box speed 400 this week but thinking about pushing and have no idea what I'm doing 😭
still on the homebrew Rodinal split. genuinely the most cost-effective thing I've found, about 30p per roll if you batch it. lmk if you want the ratios 👍

In my experience, Kodak HC-110 at dilution B handles the push to 800 cleanly without the blocked highlights you get from other options. The thing people miss about push processing is that it compensates for underexposure. It is not an aesthetic choice in itself.

Also want to raise something before we start: we had two members miss sessions last month with no way to follow the critiques. Looking at a scan-sharing trial, where anyone who prints also produces a scan at 2400 dpi minimum. Thoughts? 🙂
makes sense to me. Otto will have thoughts on the scanning part I imagine 😄 lmk if we're putting it to a vote
in and out today, field trip this afternoon. scan-sharing would have helped me last month. I'm for it.
The scan resolution would need to be sufficient for critique. From a compositional standpoint, anything under 2400 dpi loses what matters in the grain.

I will say what needs saying. Scanning is a compromise. The tonal range in a wet print does not survive digitisation cleanly. In my experience, the print is the work. I would rather members attended. That said, I understand the practical argument.
I see.
okay but Margot 'I see' could mean anything 😂 are you against it or just... thinking?? also I fully support the scan-sharing, it feels like it would make the group more connected between sessions 🙏
lowkey think scan-sharing is a great idea, highkey would have helped when I missed the November session @everyone 🙌 also I can help people with the scanning settings if needed
The practical case is clear. My read on this is that the question is less about scanning and more about what we consider the primary object of critique.
Decision: we will trial it for one month. Anyone who prints also produces a scan at 2400 dpi minimum. Happy to help with the process. 🙂
Very well.

sessions.prior_session_summary: Session 1: Group returned after the break and shared what they shot over Christmas. Otto brought Kodak Tri-X 400 contacts from canal sessions. Sol described a twelve-hour pinhole fire escape exposure. Bex asked about posting a reference link and Otto flagged this was outside the chat's norms. Yuki and Priya both commented on the value of deliberate low-volume shooting.

sessions.topic: Critique session: Sol's work stalls without context; Callum pitches housing documentary to Fen; collective space discussion

turns.message: Morning. Critiques start at 10:30. Prints on the wall by 10:20 please. Large easel is reserved for Priya as usual. She will want the full size for those frames. 🗓️
okay but I am SO ready for today, Sol sent me a preview of the fire escape prints and I had an actual physical reaction 🥹🙏 who else is showing work?? tell me everything before I get there

anyway so the point is I have five prints from the fire escape series and two from a completely different experiment I started last week @everyone come find me before the critique starts, I want to explain the context this time rather than just pinning them

I looked at Sol's contact sheets before the session. In my experience, work that requires significant contextualisation before the viewer can engage with it is asking the context to do the work the image should do. I raise this in the spirit of critique rather than criticism.

My read on this is that the triangulation in the lower third of the long-exposure piece is unresolved. It is not clear whether the form is an accidental registration or a compositional choice. That ambiguity may be deliberate, but it is worth naming.

what is the image asking of the viewer is useful here. I looked at three of the prints and genuinely could not locate an entry point. that might be the point, but I'd want to hear Sol's thinking before I know whether the confusion is productive.
okay this is fair and I hear it. honestly the critique last month where everyone got stuck really did affect me. I went away and thought about it a lot 😔
Sol, could you walk us through what the fire escape piece was trying to do before we go further? Even two sentences. 🙂

also want to mention while I'm thinking about it. came from the collective space today instead of setting up at mine like I sometimes do. there is something about the darkroom I genuinely cannot replicate at my flat. the December session at mine had three people and two complaints about the fumes. lmk if you want the full cautionary tale 😄
CALLUM I remember you saying everyone should move to home developing and now look at you 😂 okay but genuinely glad you are here, the sessions are better when everyone shows up
In my experience, shared darkroom conditions produce more consistent results than home setups regardless of individual skill. The temperature and humidity stability alone justifies the cost.
For today's critique: are we working at any size or is there a minimum? From a compositional standpoint, anything smaller than 8x10 loses the grain structure in prints like these.
@Callum the housing story. are you still thinking about pitching that as a documentary? I've been turning it over since you mentioned it last month.
yes, have a draft brief. sending it to you now. if you are in I want to move on it this month. lmk 👍
send it. if you actually go through with it, I'm in.

anyway so the point is Nora, does the street brief for next month have to be strict street? lowkey not sure themed shoots are really my thing. highkey I just want to see what happens without a brief. no offence 😬

sessions.prior_session_summary: Session 2: Group discussed developer choices and darkroom prep. Nora proposed a scan-sharing trial for absent members. Otto objected on tonal range grounds but accepted the practical argument. Margot gave a minimal two-word response. Callum anticipated Otto's position on scanning before Otto spoke. Decision: trial scan-sharing at 2400 dpi minimum.

sessions.topic: Sol's pinhole series receives external mention; Nora revises her lo-fi stance; Yuki surprised by Margot's colour work; Sol brings written statements

turns.message: Morning. Good news before we start: Sol's fire escape pinhole series picked up a mention in the regional photography group newsletter this week. Worth acknowledging. 🙂
okay I genuinely did not know about this until this morning @Bex @Callum I am still processing?? anyway so the point is I feel very weird about it and also very happy at the same time 🥹🥹

okay but SOL THIS IS AMAZING, you actually deserve this so much!! 🎉🎉 lowkey I called it when I said those prints were your best work yet. I am absolutely not surprised and also completely losing my mind right now
genuinely your best series to date. and the cost-per-frame on pinhole paper means the economics also work out. lmk if the newsletter wants to feature more 👍

I will be honest. I've been sceptical of lo-fi processes when they read as shortcuts rather than choices. Sol's fire escape series has enough intent behind it that I have had to revise that. The context Sol provided last session made the difference. 🙂

The compositional rigour in the long-exposure pieces is more considered than the format might suggest. In my experience, the strongest lo-fi work succeeds despite the process rather than because of it. The result here is notable.

I also brought written statements this time. one per print, pinned next to each one on the wall. thought it might help people find a way into the work before we start. anyway so the point is: try reading them first 🙂

okay but Sol this is so thoughtful and I'm actually moved 🥹 also I've been shooting with my Canonet all week and I finally feel like I actually know what I'm doing with it. something clicked this roll
That Canonet was the frame that clicked for you. I remember handing you mine for that afternoon session and you got six keepers on one roll. I knew you would buy your own the following week. 🙂
I brought a colour roll from the market last Saturday. First one in three years. I rather think it surprised me more than it will surprise anyone else.

I looked at Margot's prints before the session. The palette has a restraint I had not expected from colour work. Each frame is held together by a single dominant tone. My read on this is that the film choice was deliberate.

Colour darkroom work is technically demanding in ways that reward preparation. The thing people miss about RA-4 processing is the temperature sensitivity. One degree off and the balance shifts. Margot's work holds, which is not a given.
From a compositional standpoint, the negative space in the market series carries weight. The colour is the atmosphere rather than the subject. That is a useful distinction.
what is the colour asking of the viewer in those prints. I think it is asking for patience rather than impact. interesting for a market setting.
genuinely had no expectations for colour work from this group. lmk if Margot is selling any of those 😄

sessions.prior_session_summary: Session 3: Critique session. Sol's pinhole work stalled during critique and Nora asked Sol to walk through the intent. Callum noted the darkroom is irreplaceable after a poor-turnout flat session in December. Nora had pre-booked the large easel for Priya. Callum pitched a housing documentary to Fen; she committed if he followed through. Sol signalled discomfort with the upcoming themed street brief.

sessions.topic: Yuki's colour prints on the wall; Otto shifts stance; Priya's first figures roll

turns.message: Morning. Yuki's colour prints are on the wall. They have been in the fix bath since Thursday so the surface is stable. Worth looking closely before we start the critique. next session: Saturday the 8th, 10am 🗓️
okay but I walked in and STOPPED IN THE DOORWAY because these prints are so good 🥹🥹 Yuki I am actually speechless. lowkey weren't you strictly black and white for like two years?? what happened??

My read on this is that the decision was Margot's indirectly. The restraint in her market roll showed me that colour could serve the image without dominating it. I shot two rolls. These are the only frames I kept.

I want to say something carefully: this is the most controlled colour darkroom work I have seen from this group. The thing people miss about RA-4 printing is that the technical achievement is restraint, not saturation. Yuki has understood that.
Agreed. Otto, that means something coming from you. 🙂
Quite.
highkey did not expect to feel this way about colour work but lowkey here I am @Bex @Callum the shadows in the second one are incredible 🔥 this group keeps doing this to me
I want to show something today as well. I shot a roll last week that is different from my usual approach. There are figures in every frame.
interested. what is the image asking of those figures. subjects or structure? and what prompted the shift?

I've always thought of figures as compositional interruptions. The work Fen showed last session changed that. I arrived today with a roll that treats the figures as structural elements rather than as interruptions.

genuinely did not see that coming from you Priya. the geometry in those frames is different, the figures are load-bearing in a way the empty shots never were. lmk if you are printing the whole series 👍
The diagonal created by the figure in the third frame resolves the tension in the negative space. My read on this is that the shift was not just thematic. The compositional logic changed.

In my experience, figural work forces a different kind of commitment from the photographer. You cannot correct for it in the darkroom the way you can correct for light. Priya's prints show that understanding.
okay but THIS is exactly what I mean about this group 🥹 everyone keeps surprising each other. also Priya can I ask about the film stock because the grain in these is genuinely beautiful
Good session. See everyone Saturday. next session: Saturday the 8th, 10am 🗓️

sessions.prior_session_summary: Session 4: Sol's pinhole series got an external newsletter mention. Nora acknowledged she had revised her scepticism about lo-fi processes after Sol's work. Sol brought written statements for each print. Nora recalled lending Bex her Canonet and knew Bex would buy her own. Margot showed her first colour roll in three years; Yuki observed the palette had restraint they had not expected from colour work.

sessions.topic: Scan-sharing workflow formalised; Margot's stance shifts; practical resolution and grain discussion

turns.message: Morning. Practical note: two members were not at the last session. As we agreed, scanning is the only way to include them in the critique. If you printed last week, please send a scan to the shared folder by Wednesday. 2400 dpi minimum. 🗓️
already scanned mine!! they are not perfect scans but I thought it was better to send something than nothing. Fen yours are in the shared folder 📁🙏
I will send the contacts. Not the prints. In my experience the print is what matters, but I understand the practicality. The tonal range will read differently on screen.

Nora explained the situation. Two members unable to attend. Scanning as the only way to include them in the critique. I suppose that is different from scanning as a general practice. It serves a purpose here.
Thank you Margot. That is exactly the distinction. 🙂
Epson V600 hits 2400 fine and the cost is manageable. genuinely the best option at that price point. lmk if anyone needs the settings 👍
The grain structure in my prints does not hold cleanly above 2400. My read on this is that the scan resolution should be agreed per print rather than set as a blanket standard.
@everyone @Bex @Callum this is so exciting honestly, lowkey the scan-sharing means I can show process mid-project rather than waiting for the session!! highkey this changes how the group works 🎉
dropping in late. just caught up on the thread. appreciated the scans, genuinely. the grain read well enough to critique the two frames I was most uncertain about.
From a compositional standpoint, the scan resolution does affect readability of fine detail. Worth agreeing a minimum standard per print type rather than a single number.
I rather think the grain translation is the real question. Whether it holds through the digital intermediate or whether we are critiquing a facsimile. That is worth sitting with.

The thing people miss about digital scanning of silver gelatin prints is the compression of tonal range in the midtones. The shadows flatten first. Worth keeping in mind when reading scans critically.

okay but can someone explain the settings to me like I'm five because I genuinely don't know what I'm doing with the software. what bit depth?? what colour profile?? greyscale or RGB for black and white prints?? 😭😭
16-bit greyscale. Adobe RGB if you insist on a colour profile. 2400 dpi minimum. genuinely the settings I use every time. lmk if you need a walkthrough 👍
Good. Let's move into printing. next session: Saturday the 15th, 10am 🗓️

sessions.prior_session_summary: Session 5: Yuki presented colour darkroom prints. Otto called them the most controlled colour work he had seen from the group. Priya showed a figures roll, noting that Fen's documentary work from the previous session changed how she thought about people in frames. Both Otto's colour stance and Priya's compositional approach had visibly evolved.

sessions.topic: Fen and Callum share early housing documentary prints; end-of-season show discussion begins

turns.message: Morning. Callum and Fen have been in the field for the housing documentary project. They are going to show some early prints today. Worth paying attention. 🙂
went out twice in the last two weeks with Fen. genuinely the most focused work I have done in a year. three rolls of Kodak Tri-X 400 and shot slow. lmk after if you want to see the contact sheets 👍

three weeks into this now. Callum pitched a housing story I thought would stay at the idea stage. It did not. Arguably the strongest editorial work I've done since leaving full-time staff. It needed a second perspective to exist at all.

okay but this is so exciting, the way you two are describing it sounds like the whole is genuinely bigger than the parts 🥹🙏 I want to see everything. also I feel like I watched this collaboration start from nothing

In my experience, documentary collaboration requires a clearly agreed division of editorial authority. The thing people miss about joint projects is that aesthetic disagreements are manageable but curatorial disagreements are not. I would be interested to hear how you have navigated that.

My read on this is that the question of authorship in collaborative documentary work is less about division and more about intent alignment. Whether both contributors are asking the same question of the image.
anyway so the point is @Callum @Fen are these going to be part of the end of season show?? because highkey they should be and lowkey I think this is the anchor work 🔥
From a compositional standpoint, joint work can obscure individual voice. I would be curious whether you can tell whose frames are whose without context.
Very Salgado in what I can see from here. I rather think the stillness in the third print is the most considered frame of the group.

what the project is asking of us is a useful frame. the housing is the subject, not the people. when we disagree it's about whether a frame is doing that or not. arguably that is the only useful editorial question.

genuinely the best collaborative experience I've had, and I'm not prone to saying that. Fen kept me honest about the editorial line every time I drifted toward the interesting shot rather than the right one. lmk if anyone wants to follow the project as it develops 👍
This is what the collective is for. Exactly this. Let us talk about the end of season show. I think the housing work should anchor it. 🙂

okay but YES and can we also talk about whether we submit externally?? like is this the kind of work that goes somewhere bigger?? I have about three questions about the logistics and also one about whether I am allowed to submit my Canonet roll 😭🙏
highkey think we should do something public with this. lowkey been thinking about the pinhole series and whether it holds up for a wall @everyone 🔥
In my experience, the decision of whether a body of work is ready for public showing requires distance from the making of it. I would caution against rushing the timeline.

sessions.prior_session_summary: Session 6: Scan-sharing workflow formalised. Margot accepted scanning as valid for absent members, distinguishing it from scanning as general practice. Practical discussion about bit depth, resolution and grain translation. Callum provided settings guidance for Bex. Nora set next session date.

sessions.topic: End of spring season: exhibition planning, print format decisions, next season dates

turns.message: Morning. Last session of the spring run. Darkroom is booked through to June. Show date proposal: Saturday the 26th of April at the arts centre. I will confirm the space this week. next session: Saturday the 5th of April, 10am 🗓️
okay but before logistics can we actually talk about the show?? I've been thinking about it all week and I have thoughts and also fears 😭🙏 who is submitting and what format are we going with??

anyway so the point is I want to show the pinhole fire escape series. the statements I wrote for each one actually made me understand the work better than I did when I made it. @Nora @Bex @everyone what wall size are we working with? 🔥
cost per large print at the digital lab is about twelve pounds per A2. genuinely better than going through the collective budget for this run. lmk if you want the quote 👍
I rather think a flat presentation suits what this group produces. Each print should speak for itself without editorial sequencing doing the work for it.
From a compositional standpoint, the hanging layout carries as much meaning as the prints themselves. The proximity between frames creates a reading that is not present in the individual image.
My read on this is that the adjacency of Priya's architecture series and the housing documentary work creates a reading that neither has alone. The geometric and the social in tension.

The thing people miss about group exhibitions is variation in print quality between members. In my experience, consistent paper type and tonal range across the show matters more than the individual selection.
arguably the work tells you where it wants to hang. the housing prints want to be near each other and near the floor. they are not wall-centre images.
These are exactly the conversations I wanted us to have. Technically speaking, the arts centre wall is 6 metres across and the ceiling is high, so we have room to be deliberate about it. 🙂
okay but also, if this exhibition gives me a deadline I am submitting my first medium format roll. I've been putting it off for months and I think I am finally ready. lowkey terrified though 😭
genuinely the right call Bex. first medium format roll for the show is worth it for the learning alone. lmk if you need a development walkthrough 👍
@Bex lowkey you are going to be incredible with medium format. highkey I've been watching your 35mm improve all year and it's so obvious you are ready 🥹🔥
Yes.

Good session. Good group. See you all in April. still not happy with how the shadows came out on my own prints this month, but that is what next season is for. next session: Saturday the 5th of April, 10am 🗓️
